original_test_intent: Validate that each GPU's Inforom is readable and healthy through the approved DCGM diagnostic without changing persistent identity, firmware/configuration metadata or checksums.
original_method: Record GPU UUID/serial/firmware and supported Inforom fields, object versions and health/checksum status; verify DCGM operation is read-only; preserve logs; establish service/persistence in supported order; run the complete monitored level-4 diagnostic once; compare metadata byte/field identity and health before/after and escalate any write or corruption indication.
manual_activity: GPU firmware owner approves readable Inforom fields, health/checksum oracle and read-only diagnostic semantics; operator authorizes isolated runtime changes and owns vendor escalation.
required_inputs: Vendor Inforom field, version and health documentation
Confirmation that selected diagnostic performs no writes
Isolation, OOB, stop and recovery plan
safety_requirements: Never write or repair Inforom during this test
Use authenticated access and full output
Stop on mismatch and do not retry automatically
agent_execution_scope: Restore runtime state and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve field/checksum oracle and read-only semantics

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It neither measures Inforom nor proves a no-write boundary and also conflicts on level, truncates output and weakens remote security.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After vendor confirmation of read-only behavior, capture supported per-GPU Inforom state, start DCGM correctly and retain the full level-4 Inforom result plus identical post-state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Level 4, persistence change, 30-minute machine allowance and all-tests-PASS criterion are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use per-GPU persistent metadata identity and health/checksum comparisons around the named DCGM subtests with a strict no-write boundary.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds Inforom-specific fields, immutable baseline and corruption recovery gate.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A suite-level PASS without metadata comparison does not prove Inforom integrity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Inforom corruption can affect device identity, firmware state and serviceability and must not be repaired by an automatic retry.

project_override_considerations: Firmware engineering must specify which Inforom objects exist on each GPU generation and which unreadable/unsupported fields are acceptable skips versus failures.
expected_evidence: Pre/post supported Inforom fields, object versions and health/checksums
Complete level-4 output and relevant subtests
Unchanged metadata, final health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source orders service after diagnostic, DeepSeek asks for level-1 evidence for a level-4 source command, and the generic criterion omits the Inforom state and no-write oracle named by Items.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution blocks when supported Inforom fields, read-only semantics, recovery, compatible tooling or safe isolation cannot be proven.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row360 Wistron-NV GPU-00353-V002: approve per-GPU Inforom fields/object versions/health-checksum oracle, confirmed read-only level-4 behavior and vendor recovery, service-first order, source level-4 over DeepSeek level-1, final persistence/service state and handling of unsupported fields.

review_improvement: Makes persistent metadata integrity—not just a generic diagnostic status—the acceptance basis and prohibits unintended writes.
independent_technical_reasoning: Inforom is persistent device metadata, so a diagnostic result is trustworthy only when the intended fields are readable and identical afterward. Any unexplained checksum, identity or object-version change has a larger blast radius than a transient plugin error and requires preservation and vendor review, not rerun.
